degree_required.quote: The applicant shall possess the degree of doctor of medicine or doctor of osteopathy or its equivalent from a medical school which was approved by the board as of the time the degree was conferred.

exams.name: Examination for licensure
exams.notes: Board shall prepare and give, or approve the preparation and giving of, an examination. Applicant must achieve a passing score. Up to 2 subsequent attempts (3 total) within 19 months of first exam before additional requirements may apply.
exams.quote: The board shall: (1) adopt rules concerning examinations; and (2) prepare and give, or approve the preparation and giving of, an examination which covers those general subjects and topics

exams.name: United States Medical Licensing Examination (USMLE) or Comprehensive Osteopathic Medical Licensing Examination (COMLEX)
exams.notes: Required for interstate compact expedited licensure eligibility; passed each component within three attempts.
exams.quote: Passed each component of the United States Medical Licensing Examination or the Comprehensive Osteopathic Medical Licensing Examination within three (3) attempts

interval_years.quote: a license issued under this article expires biennially on the date established by the licensing agency under IC 25-1-5-4.

required.quote: Physicians shall comply with all continuing professional development or continuing medical education requirements for renewal of a license issued by a member state.

available.quote: The board in its discretion may register as a physician and may issue by endorsement an unlimited license to practice medicine or osteopathic medicine to any applicant who has: (1) complied with the minimum requirements of IC 25-22.5-3; and (2) passed an examination: (A) for licensure in another state or territory of the United States, or Canada

requirements.value: Applicant must have complied with the minimum requirements of IC 25-22.5-3 and passed an equivalent examination for licensure in another state or territory of the United States or Canada, or by a recognized certifying agency approved by the board. Board has discretion to refuse or issue probationary license if applicant was disciplined in another jurisdiction.
requirements.quote: The board in its discretion may register as a physician and may issue by endorsement an unlimited license to practice medicine or osteopathic medicine to any applicant who has: (1) complied with the minimum requirements of IC 25-22.5-3; and (2) passed an examination: (A) for licensure in another state or territory of the United States, or Canada; or (B) given by a recognized certifying agency approved by the board; if that examination was, in the opinion of the board, equivalent in every respect to Indiana's examination at the time it was taken.

exists.quote: The medical licensing board of Indiana is created. It shall consist of seven (7) members

national_association.quote: it shall include residency training or certification approved by a national association founded in 1897 that accredits residency training programs and certifying boards for osteopathic physicians as criteria that satisfy the requirement.

credential_type.quote: Issue an unlimited license, a limited license, or a temporary medical permit, depending upon the qualifications of the applicant, to any applicant who successfully fulfills all of the requirements of this article.

title_protection.quote: Attaching to a name, either alone or in connection with other words, the designation or term: (A) "doctor of medicine"; (B) "M.D."; (C) "doctor of osteopathy"; (D) "D.O."; (E) "physician"

scope_protection.quote: It is unlawful for any person to practice medicine or osteopathic medicine in this state without holding a license or permit to do so, as provided in this article.

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Improper termination of a physician and patient relationship.

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Practicing with an expired medical license.

disciplinary_grounds.quote: Providing office based anesthesia without the proper accreditation.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to perform duties required for issuing birth or death certificates
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to perform duties required for issuing birth or death certificates.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to disclose, or negligent omission of, documentation requested for licensure renewal
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to disclose, or negligent omission of, documentation requested for licensure renewal.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to complete or timely transmit a pregnancy termination form
disciplinary_grounds.quote: Failure to complete or timely transmit a pregnancy termination form under IC 16-34-2-5, with each failure constituting a separate violation.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Knowingly participating in or attempting cloning
disciplinary_grounds.quote: the board shall revoke the license of a physician if, after appropriate notice and an opportunity for a hearing, the attorney general proves by a preponderance of the evidence that the physician knowingly participated in cloning or attempted cloning.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to transmit pregnancy termination form to the Indiana Department of Health
disciplinary_grounds.quote: may revoke the license of a physician if, after appropriate notice and an opportunity for a hearing, the attorney general proves by a preponderance of the evidence that the physician failed to transmit the form to the Indiana department of health as described in IC 16-34-2-5(b)

disciplinary_grounds.description: Performing an abortion in violation of certain statutes with intent to avoid statutory requirements
disciplinary_grounds.quote: shall revoke the license of a physician if, after appropriate notice and an opportunity for a hearing, the attorney general proves by a preponderance of the evidence that the physician performed an abortion in violation of IC 16-34-2-7(a) through IC 16-34-2-7(c) with the intent to avoid the requirements of IC 16-34-2-1.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Knowingly or intentionally practicing medicine or osteopathic medicine without a license
disciplinary_grounds.quote: A person who knowingly or intentionally violates this article by unlawfully practicing medicine or osteopathic medicine commits a Class C felony (for a crime committed before July 1, 2014) or a Level 5 felony (for a crime committed after June 30, 2014).

disciplinary_grounds.description: Having a conviction for a crime that has a direct bearing on the applicant's ability to practice competently
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The applicant must not have a conviction for a crime that has a direct bearing on the applicant's ability to practice competently.

disciplinary_grounds.description: Having had disciplinary action taken by the board or licensing agency of any other state for inability to safely practice
disciplinary_grounds.quote: The applicant shall not have had disciplinary action taken against the applicant or the applicant's license by the board or by the licensing agency of any other state or jurisdiction by reasons of the applicant's inability to safely practice medicine or osteopathic medicine

disciplinary_grounds.description: Failure to comply with a protocol developed by the medical licensing board for experimental or nonconventional treatments
disciplinary_grounds.quote: A physician who fails to comply with a protocol developed under this subsection shall be subject to discipline by the medical licensing board.

definition_quote.value: "Practice of medicine or osteopathic medicine" means any one (1) or a combination of the following: (1) Holding oneself out to the public as being engaged in: (A) the diagnosis, treatment, correction, or prevention of any disease, ailment, defect, injury, infirmity, deformity, pain, or other condition of human beings; (B) the suggestion, recommendation, or prescription or administration of any form of treatment, without limitation; (C) the performing of any kind of surgical operation upon a human being...; or (D) the prevention of any physical, mental, or functional ailment or defect of any person.
definition_quote.quote: "Practice of medicine or osteopathic medicine" means any one (1) or a combination of the following: (1) Holding oneself out to the public as being engaged in: (A) the diagnosis, treatment, correction, or prevention of any disease, ailment, defect, injury, infirmity, deformity, pain, or other condition of human beings

value: telehealth / electronic diagnostic or treatment services
methods_authorized.quote: the diagnosis, treatment, correction, or prevention of any disease, ailment, defect, injury, infirmity, deformity, pain, or other condition of human beings; (B) the suggestion, recommendation, or prescription or administration of any form of treatment, without limitation; (C) the performing of any kind of surgical operation upon a human being

drug_authority.value: Physicians may prescribe, direct, order, or designate the use of drugs, medicines, or treatments. Prescribing of controlled substances is subject to board rules and statutory limits including opioid prescribing limitations.
drug_authority.quote: "Prescribe or prescription" means to direct, order, or designate the use of or manner of using a drug, medicine, or treatment, by spoken or written words or other means and in accordance with IC 25-1-9.3.

license_status_types.quote: Issue an unlimited license, a limited license, or a temporary medical permit, depending upon the qualifications of the applicant

foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.value: Foreign medical graduates must meet all requirements of Section 1 of Chapter 3 (except subsection (i)) plus complete a minimum of two years of postgraduate training in a US or Canadian hospital or institution meeting standards approved by nationally recognized medical or osteopathic accrediting bodies. The board may waive the second year of postgraduate training.
foreign_medical_graduate_requirements.quote: an applicant for licensure who: (1) has been graduated from a medical school outside the United States, its possessions, or Canada; and (2) submits evidence satisfactory to the board that prior to passing the examination the applicant has successfully completed a minimum of at least two (2) years of postgraduate training in a hospital or an institution located in the United States or Canada which meets the standards approved by the nationally recognized medical or osteopathic accrediting bodies in the United States

postgraduate_training_years_required.quote: The applicant shall have completed one (1) year of postgraduate training in a hospital or institution located in the United States, its possessions, or Canada that meets standards set by the board under IC 25-22.5-2-7.

opioid_prescribing_limits.value: The board shall adopt rules setting forth conditions exempted from prescribing limitations under IC 25-1-9.7-2(a). Rules establishing standards and protocols for prescribing controlled substances are required. Prescribing methadone for pain must include notation that it is for pain treatment.
opioid_prescribing_limits.quote: the medical licensing board of Indiana shall, in consultation with the Indiana department of health, the office of the secretary of family and social services, and representatives of prescriber stakeholders, adopt rules under IC 4-22-2 setting forth the conditions the board considers necessary under IC 25-1-9.7-2(b)(1)(D) to be exempted from the prescribing limitations set forth in IC 25-1-9.7-2(a).

controlled_substance_database_registrati.quote: "INSPECT program" means the Indiana scheduled prescription electronic collection and tracking program established by IC 25-1-13-4.

telehealth_prescribing_rules.value: The board may adopt rules under IC 4-22-2 establishing guidelines for the practice of telehealth in Indiana. Telehealth is included in the definition of practice of medicine when diagnostic or treatment services are transmitted through electronic communications on a regular, routine, and nonepisodic basis or under an oral or written agreement to regularly provide medical services.
telehealth_prescribing_rules.quote: Providing diagnostic or treatment services to a person in Indiana when the diagnostic or treatment services: (A) are transmitted through electronic communications; and (B) are on a regular, routine, and nonepisodic basis or under an oral or written agreement to regularly provide medical services.

interstate_medical_licensure_compact_mem.quote: Administer the interstate medical licensure compact under IC 25-22.5-16, including appointing members to the interstate medical licensure compact commission and adopting any rules necessary to administer the compact.

physician_assistant_supervision_model.quote: "Physician assistant" means an individual who: (1) has a collaborative agreement with a physician

malpractice_reporting_required.quote: The applicant shall be physically and mentally capable of, and professionally competent to, safely engage in the practice of medicine or osteopathic medicine as determined by the board and shall submit: (1) to an examination; or (2) additional evidence to the board; if considered necessary by the board to determine such capability. In making that determination, the board may consider any malpractice settlements or judgments against the applicant.

compelled_mental_physical_exam_authority.quote: The applicant shall be physically and mentally capable of, and professionally competent to, safely engage in the practice of medicine or osteopathic medicine as determined by the board and shall submit: (1) to an examination; or (2) additional evidence to the board; if considered necessary by the board to determine such capability.

investigational_drug_protection.quote: This section does not create a cause of action against a health care provider involved in connection with the use of an investigational drug, biological product, or device by a patient for any harm to the patient from the investigational drug, biological product, or device.
